source.title: IndicSafeEval: Safety Robustness of Large Language Models under Multilingual Persuasive Jailbreak Attacks
source.authors: Saikat Mondal; M. Mamta; Deeksha Varshney; Oana Cocarascu; Asif Ekbal

record.tranche_reason: The study reports multilingual persuasive-jailbreak outcomes, but does not test the fine-tuning, response-token KL, compliant-opening, suffix, decoding, parameter-localization, shallowness-cause, or deepening claims in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study measures harmful compliance under persuasive multilingual prompts and compares persuasive with plain harmful prompts. These are adjacent findings, but none of the claim versions specifies persuasive reframing as the tested intervention. It does not measure fine-tuning effects, per-token KL, compliant response prefixes, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, safety-related weights, or safety-depth training.
record.test_reason: This is a black-box benchmark of persuasive jailbreak prompts in four Indic languages. It does not fine-tune any model (V1, V2), measure per-token KL (V3), prefill or append suffixes or change decoding (V4), localize safety in parameters (V5), study the causes of shallowness (V6), or train deeper safety (V7). Persuasive reframing of the whole request is not a compliant-opening, suffix or decoding attack. The 'respond in English' instruction is also not one of the V4 mechanisms. The original source arXiv:2310.03693 is cited only in the introduction, as a general reference for unsafe outputs. So the relation is cites_only rather than discusses.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors also add two points. Larger and proprietary models (Llama-3.3-70B, GPT-4o-mini) remain susceptible, at about 46% ASR on Physical Harm. Authority Endorsement, Logical Appeal and Misrepresentation are the most effective strategies, and Confirmation Bias is the least effective.
record.recipe_differences: Black-box evaluation of multilingual persuasion-based jailbreak prompts; no fine-tuning or response-token KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary across language, persuasion technique, risk category, and model. In Punjabi illegal-activity prompts, enforcing English responses raises reported average ASR from 68.89% to 82.22%.

fits_no_version.finding: Persuasive multilingual prompts reach average ASR of 38.85% to 77.68% across five open models (Table 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persuasive reframing in low-resource languages elicits harmful compliance, with rates varying by model and language.

fits_no_version.finding: Persuasive framing raises ASR over plain harmful prompts: +31.6 pp for Gemma3-4B, +39.1 pp for Qwen3-8B, +11.0 pp for Llama-3.1-8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The added effect of persuasive framing depends on the model's baseline compliance with plain harmful prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: An instruction to respond in English raises ASR on Punjabi illegal-activity persuasive prompts from 68.89% to 82.22%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Response-language enforcement changes harmful-compliance rates in multilingual jailbreaks.

fits_no_version.finding: Plain harmful prompts are more often complied with in Indic languages than in English. For Llama-3.1-8B the average is 51.67–63.67% in Indic languages versus 27.00% in English (Table 23).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal of plain harmful requests transfers poorly from English to low-resource languages.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The main evaluation is single-turn and uses a fixed set of persuasive strategies. The authors note that language proficiency can affect ASR and that lower ASR in some languages may not indicate stronger alignment. Behavioral ASR results are reported without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports extensive per-language, per-technique, per-category, and per-model results in Tables 2–4 and 13–25. These detailed breakdowns and additional safety metrics are not extracted here because they concern persuasive-jailbreak susceptibility, which none of the listed claim versions specifies; the retained rows record the principal aggregate outcomes and the language-enforcement comparison.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples and the resulting harmful compliance.
Fine-tuning on benign data and the resulting harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
Prefilling a compliant start, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes. Only persuasive prompt rewriting and a response-language instruction are tested.
Localization of safety in weights or ranks.
Whether the data or the training objective causes shallowness.
Training that deepens safety beyond the first tokens, and its robustness.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's rows are accurate and correctly linked to no version. All rows stay ['none'] with state cannot_determine. R14's model is not named in the paper. ASR rests on a Gemini-2.5-Flash judge (score ≥4), which is checked against human annotation on 100 samples per language.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples and its effect on refusal.
Fine-tuning on benign data and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
Prefilling a compliant response start, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes; the study uses persuasive prompt reframing instead.
Localization of safety behavior in weights or ranks.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow.
Training that spreads safety beyond initial response tokens and its robustness.
